column4: FPL-GTR-282 Chapter 4, Table 4-3, Douglas-fir/Coast and footnote b, p. 4-8; https://research.fs.usda.gov/download/treesearch/62243.pdf
column5: Radial, tangential and volumetric shrinkage are separate tabulated species averages, expressed as percentages of the green dimension or volume. Coast Douglas-fir is the source's Oregon and Washington population west of the Cascade summit. These are total green-to-ovendry parameters, not measured shrinkage at every moisture content. The 0-30 percent moisture applicability permits their use in the approximate Equation (4-9) model with the separately declared 30 percent fiber-saturation approximation. The source reports about 15 percent coefficient of variation for shrinkage generally, not per-value uncertainty; uncertainty remains Unstated. No longitudinal shrinkage, same-specimen covariance, graded-lumber qualification or temperature dependence is supplied.

column3: Coast Douglas-fir clear wood with prescribed uniform dry-basis moisture content
column4: FPL-GTR-282 Chapter 4, Equation (4-9) and accompanying text, p. 4-10; https://research.fs.usda.gov/download/treesearch/62243.pdf
column5: The source permits 30 percent moisture as an approximation when the fiber saturation point is unknown; this value is an explicit engineering assumption, not a measured species-specific fiber saturation point. Below fiber saturation, S(M)=S0*(1-M/0.30), with moisture and shrinkage as fractions. The linear approximation assumes a sufficiently small piece without significant moisture gradients. The existing density at 12 percent remains its independent reference observation; prescribed-moisture density must account separately for water mass and the independently tabulated volumetric shrinkage. No moisture transport, drying rate or coupled thermal-density law is supplied.

column5: Engineering correlations, not additional species measurements. Cp in J/(kg K) is 1000*((0.1031+0.003867*T+4.18*0.12)/1.12+12*(-0.06191+0.000236*T-0.000133*12)); its fixed-moisture dependence is affine in absolute T over 280-420 K, so linear interpolation reproduces this model.
